# Lab 17.8: Create a Key & Use It as CMEK

## What We Are Going to Do
Create a Cloud KMS key, allow Cloud Storage to use it, and make it the default encryption key for a bucket.

## Steps

1. **Create a key ring and key.** Use the same location as the data.


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">gcloud services enable cloudkms.googleapis.com
gcloud kms keyrings create lab-ring --location=us-central1
gcloud kms keys create lab-key --keyring=lab-ring --location=us-central1 \
  --purpose=encryption --protection-level=software</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   Use `--protection-level=hsm` for keys in Cloud HSM.

2. **Let the Cloud Storage service agent use the key.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">gcloud storage service-agent \
  --authorize-cmek=projects/$PROJECT_ID/locations/us-central1/keyRings/lab-ring/cryptoKeys/lab-key</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   This grants **Cloud KMS CryptoKey Encrypter/Decrypter** to the service agent, not to people.

3. **Create a bucket with CMEK as the default.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">gcloud storage buckets create gs://$PROJECT_ID-cmek --location=us-central1 \
  --default-encryption-key=projects/$PROJECT_ID/locations/us-central1/keyRings/lab-ring/cryptoKeys/lab-key</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


4. **Upload and check an object.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">echo "encrypted with my key" | gcloud storage cp - gs://$PROJECT_ID-cmek/secret.txt
gcloud storage objects describe gs://$PROJECT_ID-cmek/secret.txt --format="value(kms_key)"</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   The output shows the key and its version.

5. **See key usage.** In **Security → Key Management**, open `lab-key` and look at its key usage view, which lists the resources the key protects.

6. **Require CMEK.** In **Organization policies**, look at **Restrict which services may create resources without CMEK** (`gcp.restrictNonCmekServices`).

7. **Keep the key** for the next lab. Delete the bucket at the end of Lab 17.11.

## Expected Result

| Thing | Reality |
|---|---|
| Object encryption | With your key, `lab-key` |
| Who uses the key | Cloud Storage service agent |
| Key location | Must match the data location |
| Key deletion | Not possible, only key versions can be destroyed |
